method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207) 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study' (published 1 April 2025). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS <license> element for PMC12026134 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 503 on 2026-09-23)).

claims.claim: **Glioblastoma has no cure;** in Canada median survival was 8.1 months and 5-year survival 4.9%.
claims.source_text: The median survival time of patients diagnosed with glioblastoma between 2010 and 2017 in Canada was only 8.1 months, and the 5-year overall survival rate was 4.9% … There are no curative treatments for glioblastoma
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Image every suspected glioblastoma with brain MRI;** use CT only if MRI is unavailable or contraindicated. Advanced MRI and PET help in difficult cases.
claims.source_text: all patients with a suspected diagnosis of glioblastoma should undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain and that computed tomography (CT) should be used to evaluate patients with suspected glioblastoma only if MRI is unavailable or contraindicated. … A moderate consensus was achieved regarding the use of advanced brain MRI techniques, such as diffusion-weighted MRI and perfusion-weighted MRI, positron emission tomography (PET), and magnetic resonance (MR) spectroscopy, to assess the presence of glioblastoma in difficult cases or to help distinguish glioblastoma from other tumor types and progression from radionecrosis.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Under WHO 2021, only IDH-wildtype grade 4 gliomas are glioblastoma.** An adult IDH-wildtype astrocytic glioma counts as glioblastoma if it shows microvascular proliferation, necrosis, TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification or +7/−10 changes.
claims.source_text: In accordance with the 2021 WHO classification criteria, the panelists reached a strong consensus that only IDH-wildtype grade 4 gliomas should be classified as glioblastoma and that IDH-wildtype astrocytic gliomas in adults should be considered glioblastoma if any of the following criteria are met: microvascular proliferation, necrosis, TERT promoter mutation, EGFR gene amplification, and +7/-10 chromosome copy number changes.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test every new glioma for IDH mutation,** and test MGMT promoter methylation in glioblastoma to inform prognosis and predict temozolomide benefit.
claims.source_text: Panelists reached a strong consensus that all patients with newly diagnosed gliomas should be tested (by immunohistochemistry or sequencing) for IDH mutations. … MGMT promoter methylation status should be tested to inform prognosis and predict response to temozolomide chemotherapy.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Management is palliative from the outset:** discuss goals of care with patient and family; palliative care alone is reasonable when performance status is very poor.
claims.source_text: Considering that the intent of management is palliative or non-curative from the outset, the panelists agreed that part of the discussion on further management should involve conversations with the patient and their family about the goals of care and whether they wish to proceed with active therapies. For some patients with a very poor performance status, palliative care alone is a reasonable option.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Base first-line choice on tumour size, location and integrated diagnosis, and on age, KPS, symptoms and preferences,** within a multidisciplinary team.
claims.source_text: when deciding the first-line treatment for patients with glioblastoma, clinicians must take into account the tumor characteristics (size, location, and integrated diagnosis) and the patient's age, functional ability measured as Karnofsky performance status (KPS), symptoms, clinical needs, and preferences.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maximal safe resection for operable tumours with good performance status;** stereotactic biopsy when resection is not possible, and bank tissue where feasible.
claims.source_text: all patients with newly diagnosed operable glioblastoma and those with good performance status should undergo maximal safe resection. … stereotactic biopsy is recommended to establish a histopathologic diagnosis and molecular profile (including cytogenetic alterations). The panelists also agreed that tissue should be saved for tumor banking whenever feasible.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start radiotherapy as soon as safe, ideally 3–6 weeks after surgery.**
claims.source_text: radiation therapy should be initiated as soon as it is safely permissible, ideally within 3-6 weeks after surgery
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Age 70 or under with KPS 60 or more:** 60 Gy radiotherapy with concurrent temozolomide 75 mg/m² for 42 days, then adjuvant temozolomide 150–200 mg/m² on 5 of every 28 days for six cycles.
claims.source_text: Consensus was reached regarding the use of 75 mg/m2 concurrently with 60 Gy radiotherapy for 42 days, followed by adjuvant temozolomide 150-200 mg/m2 in a 5/28-day schedule for six cycles in patients aged ≤ 70 years with good performance status (KPS ≥60).
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Temozolomide benefit is concentrated in MGMT-methylated tumours;** extending adjuvant temozolomide beyond six cycles did not improve survival in a recent meta-analysis, and the panel did not agree on 12 months.
claims.source_text: no survival benefit with temozolomide addition was observed in patients with unmethylated tumors … continuing adjuvant temozolomide beyond six cycles did not increase PFS or OS … There was no consensus regarding the extension of maintenance therapy up to 12 months
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Over 70 with KPS 60 or more:** 40 Gy hypofractionated radiotherapy with temozolomide 75 mg/m² for 21 days, then adjuvant temozolomide 150–200 mg/m² (5 of 28 days) for 6–12 cycles. Older patients with truly unmethylated MGMT may gain nothing from temozolomide.
claims.source_text: For patients aged > 70 years with a good performance status (KPS ≥ 60), the panelists recommend 40 Gy hypofractionated radiotherapy plus concurrent temozolomide 75 mg/m2 for 21 days, followed by adjuvant temozolomide 150-200 mg/m2 in a 5/28-day schedule for 6-12 cycles. … suggests no benefit from temozolomide treatment for older (>60 years old) patients with glioblastoma with truly unmethylated MGMT promoter
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **KPS under 60:** hypofractionated radiotherapy (25 Gy/5, 34 Gy/10 or 40 Gy/15) with or without temozolomide, temozolomide alone only if MGMT-methylated, or palliative care alone.
claims.source_text: the use of hypofractionated radiotherapy with or without concurrent or adjuvant temozolomide, temozolomide alone (only in the presence of MGMT methylation), or palliative care alone in patients with a poor performance status (KPS < 60). Options for hypofractionated radiotherapy include 25 Gy in 5 fractions, 34 Gy in 10 fractions, or 40 Gy in 15 fractions with or without temozolomide
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tumour-treating fields can be added to adjuvant temozolomide** after chemoradiation for KPS 60 or more, whatever the MGMT status; EF-14 improved median survival from 16.0 to 20.9 months.
claims.source_text: The panelists reached a consensus regarding the combination of TTFields with adjuvant temozolomide after treatment with standard chemoradiotherapy for patients with a good performance status (KPS ≥ 60), regardless of MGMT promoter methylation status. … Data from the phase 3 EF-14 trial … OS (20.9 months vs. 16.0 months
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MRI 4–6 weeks after radiotherapy, then every 2–4 months on treatment;** assess recurrence with gadolinium MRI and RANO criteria.
claims.source_text: tumor progression or recurrence should be monitored using gadolinium-enhanced MRI, and tumor recurrence should be determined according to the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) Working Group criteria. … performing a brain MRI 4-6 weeks after radiotherapy, then every 2-4 months while on treatment
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Beware pseudoprogression:** do not call progression on MRI in the first 12 weeks after radiotherapy unless new enhancement lies outside the field or pathology confirms tumour; keep adjuvant temozolomide going when pseudoprogression is suspected.
claims.source_text: patients receiving chemoradiation should not be classified as having tumor progression based on gadolinium-enhanced MRI within the first 12 weeks after the end of radiotherapy, unless new enhancement is evident outside the radiotherapy field, or the presence of a viable tumor is confirmed by a pathologist at the time of reoperation. … They also recommend the continuation of adjuvant temozolomide in patients with suspected PsPD.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No standard of care exists at recurrence:** individualise, and encourage clinical trial entry for everyone.
claims.source_text: There is no acknowledged standard of care for patients with progressive glioblastoma. … clinical trial participation should be encouraged for all patients with recurrent disease.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reoperate only with KPS over 70 and a favourable tumour location;** re-irradiation suits selected small, favourably placed tumours long after prior treatment.
claims.source_text: repeat surgery should be considered only for patients with a high-performance status score (KPS > 70) and those with a tumor in a favorable location … Re-irradiation has long been offered as a salvage therapy for recurrent glioblastoma and should be considered in select patients, such as those with a small tumor size, a favorable tumor location, a good performance status, and a long time since previous treatment.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lomustine or temozolomide rechallenge may help some patients;** bevacizumab may be added to chemotherapy in selected patients, but adding it to lomustine did not improve survival.
claims.source_text: The panelists agreed that lomustine and rechallenge with temozolomide may benefit some patients with recurrent glioblastoma. … the addition of bevacizumab to lomustine did not improve OS compared with lomustine alone … the panelists reached a consensus that bevacizumab may be added to chemotherapy in select patients.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider targeted therapy or immunotherapy for actionable alterations** such as BRAF V600E, NTRK fusions or MSI-high.
claims.source_text: targeted therapy and immunotherapy could be considered for the management of recurrence in patients with specific genetic alterations such as BRAF V600E mutation, NTRK fusions, and high microsatellite instability (MSI-H).
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat seizures with antiepileptic drugs** (e.g. levetiracetam, lacosamide, perampanel), and screen early for depression and refer; consider rehabilitation.
claims.source_text: treatment with antiepileptic drugs (e.g., levetiracetam, lacosamide, and perampanel) should be considered for patients who experience seizures. … patients with signs of depression should be referred to a specialist for evaluation and treatment. They also agreed that rehabilitation may be considered for select patients with glioblastoma.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The panel did not agree on PJP prophylaxis during temozolomide (23%) or LMWH VTE prophylaxis after resection (46%).**
claims.source_text: The largest disagreement was related to prophylaxis for pneumocystis pneumonia in patients receiving chemoradiotherapy or adjuvant chemotherapy with temozolomide (consensus level: 23%) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis with low-molecular-weight heparin after surgical tumor resection (consensus level: 46%).
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary expert panel, Current Oncology (MDPI; doi 10.3390/curroncol32040207), 'Canadian Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Diagnosis and Management of Glioblastoma: Results of a Delphi Study', published 1 April 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12026134/, retrieved 2026-09-23
